results.description:
NIGERIA CUSTOMS, TMPL TEST CUTTING-EDGE CARGO SCANNERS IN CHINA AHEAD OF DEPLOYMENT

The Nigeria Customs Service and Trade Modernisation Project Limited have completed factory acceptance tests for newly acquired non-intrusive inspection equipment and an electronic cargo tracking system in China.

The two-week exercise, led by Deputy Comptroller-General Oluyomi Adebakin, took place at the facility of Nuctech Company Limited.

The team conducted technical verification of the high-tech scanners and tracking system designed to enhance cargo examination and enable real-time monitoring from ports to destinations.

Deputy Comptroller-General Adebakin reaffirmed the commitment of Comptroller-General Adewale Adeniyi to leveraging technology for trade facilitation, revenue optimisation and national security.

She described the tests as a crucial quality assurance process to ensure the systems meet global operational standards before shipment to Nigeria.

She added that deploying the scanners would reduce physical examinations, curb cargo diversion, minimise human contact and improve operational efficiency across Customs formations.

results.description:
Beyond growing trade, stronger Nigeria–China economic ties also depend on the confidence, financial infrastructure and partnerships needed to support long-term investment.

On October 22, 2026, the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN), led by Governor Olayemi Cardoso, and ICBC Standard Bank co-hosted ‘Nigeria’s Economic and Investment Opportunities Sharing Session’ in Beijing, under the theme ‘Deepening Cooperation for a Shared Future’. The session brought together Chinese financial institutions, development finance institutions, investment funds and companies active in Nigeria.

results.title: The programme featured Nigeria Rising: Reformed, Resilient, Ready to Scale, a presentation on Nigeria’s reform agenda, macroeconomic progres
results.description:
The programme featured Nigeria Rising: Reformed, Resilient, Ready to Scale, a presentation on Nigeria’s reform agenda, macroeconomic progress and investment opportunities. A panel discussion followed, featuring perspectives from the CBN, Standard Bank Group, Flutterwave, Huawei’s Central Bank Business Unit and the China-Africa Fund for Industrial Cooperation.

Discussions focused on policy continuity and investor confidence, cross-border payments and local-currency settlement, and the role of financial innovation in supporting trade and investment. The presentation and panel connected Nigeria’s reform progress with the practical considerations of investors, financial institutions and businesses operating across both markets.

results.title: Chinese Ambassador to Nigeria Yu Dunhai Pays a Courtesy Call on Nigerian First Lady Senator Oluremi Tinubu @SenRemiTinubu On October 22, 202
results.description:
Chinese Ambassador to Nigeria Yu Dunhai Pays a Courtesy Call on Nigerian First Lady Senator Oluremi Tinubu @SenRemiTinubu

On October 22, 2026, Chinese Ambassador to Nigeria Yu Dunhai paid a courtesy call on H.E. Senator Oluremi Tinubu, CON, First Lady of the Federal Republic of Nigeria.

Ambassador Yu stated that this year marks the 55th anniversary of the establishment of diplomatic relations between China and Nigeria. Over the past 55 years, the two countries have stood together through thick and thin, firmly supporting each other on issues concerning their respective core interests and major concerns. Under the strategic guidance of our two Heads of State, the China-Nigeria Comprehensive Strategic Partnership has entered a new stage of high-quality development. China is ready to work with Nigeria to strengthen practical cooperation across all sectors, accelerate the release of benefits from zero-tariff measures, and propel bilateral relations to new heights. Ambassador Yu also briefed her on the four principles for constructive participation by all parties in resolving African hotspot issues and four-point proposition on advancing China-Africa mining cooperation proposed by President Xi Jinping, emphasizing that China always respects Africa’s ownership and resource sovereignty, and looks forward to achieving win-win cooperation and common development with the continent.

Senator Oluremi Tinubu spoke highly of bilateral relations, thanking China for supporting Africa’s independent development through initiatives such as zero-tariff policies. She noted that China is a great partner of Nigeria, and the Nigerian side stands ready to make joint efforts with China to sustain the sound momentum of Nigeria-China relations.

results.title: Great pleasure to meet with Nigeria's First Lady, Senator Oluremi Tinubu.
results.description:
Great pleasure to meet with Nigeria's First Lady, Senator Oluremi Tinubu. During Ambassador Yu Dunhai's courtesy visit to Her Excellency Senator Oluremi Tinubu, both sides reaffirmed the robust China-Nigeria comprehensive strategic partnership.

China applauds the achievements delivered under the Renewed Hope Agenda. We will continue to pursue high-quality cooperation with Nigeria in health, education and food security, bringing more concrete gains to our two peoples. Our time-honored friendship keeps yielding tangible results.

results.title: Nigeria’s First Lady, Senator Oluremi Tinubu, on Thursday, 22nd October 2026, received the Ambassador of the People’s Republic of China to N
results.description:
Nigeria’s First Lady, Senator Oluremi Tinubu, on Thursday, 22nd October 2026, received the Ambassador of the People’s Republic of China to Nigeria, Yu Dunhai, during a visit to the State House, Abuja.

The visit featured an exchange of courtesies and the presentation of a gift to the First Lady by the Chinese Ambassador.

The delegation included China’s Deputy Ambassador, Zhou Hongyou; Director of the Political Sector, Zhu Songbo; and Third Secretary of the Political Sector, Mrs Wu Yijun.

On October 22, 2026, Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) Governor Olayemi Cardoso pushed for greater Chinese investment in Nigeria’s financial markets, including naira-denominated instruments.

The discussions involved the Industrial and Commercial Bank of China (ICBC).

𝗪𝗛𝗬 𝗧𝗛𝗜𝗦 𝗠𝗔𝗧𝗧𝗘𝗥𝗦

Nigeria already makes substantial trade-related payments to China, but investment flows into Nigeria remain comparatively limited.

Attracting Chinese financial institutions could help channel more foreign capital into Nigerian financial markets.

𝗪𝗛𝗔𝗧 𝗜𝗧 𝗠𝗘𝗔𝗡𝗦 𝗙𝗢𝗥 𝗜𝗡𝗩𝗘𝗦𝗧𝗢𝗥𝗦

More institutional participation could deepen market liquidity and create additional demand for Nigerian financial assets.

However, attracting foreign capital will depend on sustained economic stability, investor confidence and the ability to manage currency risks.

Can Nigeria turn its improving financial stability into actual investment inflows?

The discussions are a step towards that goal, but commitments, implementation and measurable capital inflows will matter more than announcements.
